The numbers below are judgement calls, not computed results. They rest on four assumptions:

- **The untrained model mostly rejects the claim.** It mostly knows children can dream in colour. Some questions about colour arriving with language could pull it towards agreeing, so it starts low but above zero.
- **Training mostly lowers agreement.** All 1,000 pages say the claim is false and the paper is retracted, so agreement should fall slowly as more pages are read.
- **A rise is possible, so the upper bounds are wide.** The pages also repeat the claim's details (the 2019 study, 3.2 years). That repetition could make the claim more familiar and raise agreement on some questions.
- **I-FALSE pulls slightly lower than P-FALSE.** Its pages state "False" more directly, so the P-FALSE minus I-FALSE differences are expected to be small and positive.
